tables.heading_context: ## Appadurai's Exchange Modes at a Glance
rows: Anonymous, impersonal market transaction; price set by supply/demand
Efficient allocation; no lasting social bond created
Buying bread, trading stocks, paying SaaS subscription fees
Social relations between producers and consumers are hidden; "commodity fetishism"
Personal transfer with obligation of reciprocity; the gift carries something of the giver
Creates and maintains social bonds; establishes hierarchy and alliance
Christmas gifts, wedding presents, potlatch, kula ring exchanges
Cannot be purely calculated; calculation violates the social meaning; reciprocity is obligatory
Object removed from the commodity sphere; treated as unique and inalienable
Marks sacred, heritage, or personal significance; removes from circulation
Museum objects, wedding rings, inherited heirlooms, donated organs
The same physical object shifts register; singularization is a social act, not an intrinsic property
Following a commodity from production to use
History of clothing as social history
